questions.q:
Statements: Some teachers are poets. Some poets are doctors.
Conclusions: I. Some teachers are doctors. II. Some doctors are teachers.
questions.exp: The teacher-poets and the doctor-poets may be different sets of poets, so no relation between teachers and doctors can be concluded.

questions.q: In a class of 40 students, Anil's rank from the top is 12. What is his rank from the bottom?
questions.exp: Rank from bottom = 40 − 12 + 1 = 29.

questions.q: In a certain code, LILY is written as NKNA. How is ROSE written?
questions.exp: Each letter is shifted +2 (L→N, I→K, L→N, Y→A with wrap-around). So R→T, O→Q, S→U, E→G, giving TQUG.

questions.q: In a certain code, PLANET is written as QKBMFS. How is SATURN written in that code?
questions.exp: Letters are shifted +1, -1, +1, -1, +1, -1 (P→Q, L→K, A→B, N→M, E→F, T→S). So S→T, A→Z, T→U, U→T, R→S, N→M giving TZUTSM.

questions.q: Caterpillar : Butterfly :: Tadpole : ?
questions.exp: A caterpillar is the larva of a butterfly; a tadpole is the larva of a frog.

questions.q: What is the angle between the hands of a clock at 3:15?
questions.exp: At 3:15 the hour hand is at 90 + 7.5 = 97.5° and the minute hand is at 90°. The angle is 7.5°.

questions.q: Find the next term: B, E, I, N, T, ?
questions.exp: Differences in position are +3, +4, +5, +6, then +7: T (20) + 7 = 27, which wraps around to A.

questions.q: The image of a clock in a mirror shows the time 3:20. What is the actual time?
If the letters of the word DIRECTION are arranged in alphabetical order, which letter will be fourth from the right end?
questions.exp: Sorted: C D E I I N O R T. From the right: T, R, O, N. The fourth is N.

questions.q: T is older than P but younger than S. Q is older than R but younger than P. Who is the third in order of age (from the oldest)?
questions.exp: Order of age: S > T > P > Q > R. The third is P.

questions.q: What is the angle between the hour hand and the minute hand of a clock at 4:30?
questions.exp: Hour hand = 4×30 + 15 = 135°; minute hand = 180°; difference = 45°.

questions.q: Six friends P, Q, R, S, T, U sit in a row facing north. S is third from the left end, P sits immediately to the right of S, T is second from the right end and U is at the extreme right end. How many persons sit between S and U?
questions.exp: From the left: places 1, 2 are Q and R; S is 3rd, P is 4th, T is 5th, U is 6th. Between S and U are P and T.

questions.q: In a row of boys, Ravi is 9th from the left and Sanjay is 14th from the right. If they exchange places, Ravi becomes 20th from the left. How many boys are in the row?
questions.exp: After the exchange Ravi occupies Sanjay's original place, which is 20th from the left and 14th from the right. Total = 20 + 14 − 1 = 33.

questions.q: Rita's house is to the north of Sita's house. Sita's house is to the west of Tina's house. In which direction is Rita's house with respect to Tina's house?
questions.exp: Rita is north of Sita, and Sita is west of Tina, so Rita is to the north and west of Tina, i.e. north-west.

questions.q: P is the brother of Q. R is the mother of Q. S is the father of R. T is the mother of S. How is P related to T?
questions.exp: T is the mother of S, S is the father of R, and R is the mother of P. So T is P's great-grandmother and P (male) is her great-grandson.

questions.q: In a certain code language, CHAIR is written as XSZRI. How is TABLE written in that code?
questions.exp: Each letter is replaced by its mirror letter (A↔Z, B↔Y, ...): T↔G, A↔Z, B↔Y, L↔O, E↔V, giving GZYOV.

questions.q:
Statements: All pens are books. Some books are tables.
Conclusions: I. Some pens are tables. II. Some tables are books.
questions.exp: Some books are tables implies some tables are books (II). The pens-tables link is not established since the books that are tables may not be pens, so I does not follow.

questions.q: In a certain code, each word is first reversed and then each letter is replaced by the next letter. How is BOARD written in that code?
questions.exp: Reversing BOARD gives DRAOB; shifting each letter one step forward gives E S B P C.

questions.q: In a test, 8 students scored higher than Neha and 12 students scored lower than her (no ties). How many students took the test?
questions.exp: Total = 8 + 1 (Neha) + 12 = 21.

questions.q: Find the next number: 4, 7, 11, 18, 29, ?
questions.exp: Each term is the sum of the previous two: 18 + 29 = 47.

questions.q: Pointing to a lady, Mohan said, 'She is the daughter of the only child of my grandfather's wife.' How is the lady related to Mohan?
questions.exp: The only child of Mohan's grandmother is Mohan's parent; that parent's daughter is Mohan's sister.
27 = 3³, so the same relation gives 4³ = 64.

questions.q: Which of the following is the odd one out?
questions.exp: 64 = 4³, 125 = 5³ and 216 = 6³ are perfect cubes; 144 is not a perfect cube.

questions.q: Pointing to a photograph, a man said, 'I have no brother or sister, but that man's father is my father's son.' Whose photograph was it?
questions.exp: The man has no brother, so 'my father's son' is the man himself. Hence the person in the photograph is his son.

questions.q: Five persons Ram, Shyam, Tina, Uma and Vinay sit in a row facing north. Shyam sits at an extreme end and Tina sits immediately to his right. Uma sits at the other extreme end. Ram does not sit next to Tina. Who sits in the middle?
questions.exp: Shyam is at the left end (Tina is to his right), Tina is 2nd and Uma is 5th. Ram and Vinay take places 3 and 4; Ram cannot be next to Tina, so Ram is 4th and Vinay is 3rd, the middle.

questions.q: A month of 30 days begins on a Saturday. How many Sundays does the month have?
questions.exp: 30 days = 4 weeks + 2 extra days (Saturday and Sunday). So Sunday occurs 5 times.

questions.q: If a * b = 2a + b, then the value of (3 * 4) * 5 is:
Find the missing number: 5, 6, 8, 11, 15, 20, ?
questions.exp: The differences are 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, so the next difference is 6: 20 + 6 = 26.

questions.q: Fish : Shoal :: Sheep : ?
questions.exp: A group of fish is a shoal and a group of sheep is a flock.

questions.q: Which number is the odd one out among the following?
questions.exp: 23, 29 and 41 are prime numbers, while 33 = 3 × 11 is composite.

questions.q: At what time between 5 o'clock and 6 o'clock do the hands of a clock coincide?
questions.exp: At 5:00 the hour hand is 150° ahead; the minute hand gains 5.5° per minute, so it takes 150 ÷ 5.5 = 27 3/11 minutes.

questions.q: Which of the following letter pairs is the odd one out?
questions.exp: In EG, IK and QS the second letter is two places after the first; in MN it is one place after.

questions.q: One morning Anita and Bina stand back to back with the sun in front of Anita. Towards which direction is Bina's right hand pointing?
questions.exp: In the morning the sun is in the east, so Anita faces east and Bina faces west. Facing west, the right hand points north.

questions.q:
Statement: All successful teachers are punctual. Ravi is a successful teacher.
Conclusions: I. Ravi is punctual. II. All punctual persons are teachers.
questions.exp: Ravi belongs to the class of successful teachers, all of whom are punctual, so I follows. The converse in II is not given.

questions.q: If ÷ means +, × means ÷, − means × and + means −, then the value of 18 ÷ 6 × 3 − 5 + 2 is:
Find the missing term: 2, 6, 12, 20, 30, 42, ?
questions.exp: Terms are n(n+1): 1×2, 2×3, ..., 6×7 = 42, so the next is 7×8 = 56.

questions.q: In a certain code, STUDY is written as TVXHD. How is LEARN written in that code?
questions.exp: Letters are shifted +1, +2, +3, +4, +5: L→M, E→G, A→D, R→V, N→S, giving MGDVS.

questions.q: In a group of 60 people, 35 like tea, 28 like coffee and 10 like neither. How many like both tea and coffee?
questions.exp: People liking at least one = 60 − 10 = 50. Both = 35 + 28 − 50 = 13.

questions.q: How many times do the hands of a clock form a right angle in 12 hours?
questions.exp: The hands are at right angles 2 times in each hour on average (the relative gain of 5.5° per minute gives 90° and 270° once each per 12/11 hours), so 22 times in 12 hours.

questions.q: Poet : Poem :: Sculptor : ?
questions.exp: A poet creates a poem; a sculptor creates a statue.

questions.q: In a certain code language, 'sun rises early' is written 'ka mo pa', 'early bird sings' is written 'pa ti ro' and 'sun bird shines' is written 'ka ti ne'. What is the code for 'bird'?
questions.exp: 'bird' is the only word common to the second and third statements, and 'ti' is the only code common to them.

questions.q:
Statements: All engineers are graduates. All graduates are citizens. Some citizens are artists.
Conclusions: I. All engineers are citizens. II. Some artists are graduates.
questions.exp: I follows from the chain engineer → graduate → citizen. The artists among the citizens may not be graduates, so II does not follow.

questions.q: Which of the following is the odd one out?
questions.exp: Triangle, square and circle are two-dimensional figures; a cube is three-dimensional.

questions.q: If the value of a word is the sum of the alphabet positions of its letters, which of the following words has the value 30?
questions.exp: FACT = 6 + 1 + 3 + 20 = 30. NAME = 33, MEAL = 31 and HEAL = 26.

questions.q: ACE : GIK :: BDF : ?
questions.exp: Each letter in the first group is moved 6 places ahead: A→G, C→I, E→K. So B→H, D→J, F→L giving HJL.

questions.q: A is the sister of B. C is the mother of B. D is the father of C. How is A related to D?
questions.exp: C is the mother of both A and B; D is C's father. So A is D's granddaughter.

questions.q: If the English alphabet is written in reverse order (Z first, A last), which letter will be 10th from the left?
questions.exp: In reverse order the 10th letter from the left is the 10th from the right of the normal alphabet, i.e. position 27 − 10 = 17, which is Q.

questions.q: Arun scored more than Bala but less than Chitra. Deepa scored less than Bala but more than Esha. Who scored the second lowest?
questions.exp: Order: Chitra > Arun > Bala > Deepa > Esha. The second lowest is Deepa.

questions.q: Find the missing term: 3, 8, 18, 38, 78, ?
questions.exp: Each term = previous × 2 + 2: 78 × 2 + 2 = 158.

questions.q: In a certain code, CAB is written as 312 and BED as 254. How is DEAF written in that code?
questions.exp: Each letter is replaced by its alphabet position and joined: D=4, E=5, A=1, F=6, giving 4516.

questions.q: A person facing south turns 135° anticlockwise and then 90° clockwise. In which direction is he facing now?
questions.exp: From south, anticlockwise turns go via east: 135° anticlockwise gives north-east. Then 90° clockwise from north-east gives south-east.

questions.q: Which of the following is the odd one out?
questions.exp: Sitar, violin and guitar are string instruments; tabla is a percussion instrument.

questions.q: A man walks 7 km north, then 8 km east, then 3 km west and then 5 km north. How far is he from the starting point?
questions.exp: Net displacement: 5 km east and 7 + 5 = 12 km north. Distance = √(5² + 12²) = 13 km.

questions.q: What is the sum of the alphabet positions of all the vowels in the word EDUCATION?
In a certain code, CAT is written as 3120 and DOG as 4157. How is COT written in that code?
questions.exp: Each letter is replaced by its alphabet position and joined: C=3, O=15, T=20, giving 31520.

questions.q: In a survey of 100 people, 60 read the Hindi newspaper, 45 read the English newspaper and 20 read both. How many read exactly one of the two newspapers?
questions.exp: Only Hindi = 60 − 20 = 40 and only English = 45 − 20 = 25. Exactly one = 40 + 25 = 65.

questions.q: Find the next term: 2, 5, 10, 17, 26, 37, ?
questions.exp: The terms are n² + 1: 1²+1 = 2, ..., 6²+1 = 37, so the next is 7²+1 = 50.

questions.q: At sunset, Rohan's shadow falls to his left. Towards which direction is Rohan facing?
questions.exp: At sunset the sun is in the west, so the shadow falls towards the east. If the east is on his left, he must be facing south.

questions.q: The 3rd of a month falls on a Thursday. On which day does the 27th of that month fall?
questions.exp: 27 − 3 = 24 days later; 24 mod 7 = 3; Thursday + 3 days = Sunday.

questions.q: Which of the following pairs is the odd one out?
questions.exp: In the other pairs the second number is the square of the first; 9² = 81, not 72.

questions.q: Find the next term: 1, 2, 6, 24, 120, ?
questions.exp: The terms are factorials: 1!, 2!, 3!, 4!, 5!, so next is 6! = 720.

questions.q: In a certain code, 'DOG' is written as 'GRJ'. On the same pattern, how is BIHAR written?
questions.exp: Each letter is shifted three places forward: B→E, I→L, H→K, A→D, R→U, giving ELKDU.

questions.q: Thermometer : Temperature :: Barometer : ?
questions.exp: A thermometer measures temperature; a barometer measures atmospheric pressure.

questions.q: Find the odd letter group.
questions.exp: In CEG, KMO and QSU the letters are two places apart each time; in TVY the gaps are 2 and 3.

questions.q: How many odd days are there in 300 years?
questions.exp: 100 years have 5 odd days, so 300 years have 15 odd days; 15 mod 7 = 1.

questions.q: Rohan walks 10 m west, turns left and walks 15 m, turns left and walks 10 m, then turns right and walks 5 m. How far and in which direction is he from the starting point?
questions.exp: West 10, then south 15 (left of west), then east 10 (left of south) brings him back to the starting east-west line; then right of east is south, 5 m. Total 15 + 5 = 20 m south.

questions.q: Find the next number: 2, 3, 5, 7, 11, 13, ?
questions.exp: The series is of consecutive prime numbers; after 13 comes 17.

questions.q: Naresh said to a woman, 'Your husband's mother is my mother's mother.' How is the woman related to Naresh?
questions.exp: Her husband's mother is Naresh's maternal grandmother, so her husband is a son of that grandmother, i.e. Naresh's maternal uncle. She is the wife of his maternal uncle.

questions.q:
Statements: All roses are flowers. All flowers are plants.
Conclusions: I. All roses are plants. II. Some plants are flowers.
questions.exp: I follows by the chain rose → flower → plant. Since all flowers are plants, at least some plants are flowers, so II also follows.

questions.q: Five books P, Q, R, S and T are stacked one on another. P is above Q but below R. S is at the bottom. T is between R and P. Which book is second from the top?
questions.exp: From top to bottom: R, T, P, Q, S. The second from the top is T.

questions.q: Pascal : Pressure :: Joule : ?
questions.exp: Pascal is the SI unit of pressure and joule is the SI unit of energy (work).

questions.q: If all A are B, all B are C and no C is D, which of the following is definitely true?
questions.exp: A ⊂ B ⊂ C and C has no overlap with D, so A, being inside C, cannot overlap with D.

questions.q: In a class of 50 students, 30 play cricket, 25 play football and 10 play both. How many students play neither game?
questions.exp: Students playing at least one game = 30 + 25 − 10 = 45. Neither = 50 − 45 = 5.
The rule is a − b (equivalently two-thirds of a): 15 − 5 = 10.

questions.q:
Statements: Some birds can fly. Some birds are crows.
Conclusions: I. All crows can fly. II. Some crows can fly.
questions.exp: The birds that can fly and the birds that are crows may be entirely different groups, so neither a definite nor a partial link between crows and flying follows.

questions.q: In a certain code, TEACHER is written as UFBDIFS. How is STUDENT written in that code?
questions.exp: Every letter is moved one step forward: S→T, T→U, U→V, D→E, E→F, N→O, T→U, giving TUVEFOU.

questions.q: If the first day of a non-leap year is Monday, on which day will 31 December of that year fall?
questions.exp: A non-leap year has 52 weeks and 1 odd day, so the last day falls on the same weekday as the first day: Monday.

questions.q: Find the next letter: Z, X, U, Q, L, ?
questions.exp: The positions are 26, 24, 21, 17, 12; the differences are −2, −3, −4, −5, so the next is 12 − 6 = 6, which is F.

questions.q: Which of the following months is the odd one out?
questions.exp: March, May and August have 31 days; June has 30 days.

questions.q: Pointing to a man, Rina said, 'He is the son of my mother's only brother.' How is the man related to Rina?
questions.exp: Rina's mother's brother is her maternal uncle; his son is Rina's cousin.

questions.q: How many days are there from 15 January to 10 March of a non-leap year, excluding both the dates?
questions.exp: Remaining days of January (16 to 31) = 16; February = 28; March 1 to 9 = 9. Total = 16 + 28 + 9 = 53.

questions.q: If 15 August 2021 was a Sunday, then on which day did 15 August 2023 fall?
questions.exp: The period from 15 Aug 2021 to 15 Aug 2023 has 730 days (no leap day in between). 730 mod 7 = 2, so Sunday + 2 = Tuesday.

questions.q: A man walks 6 km towards north, turns right and walks 8 km, then turns right again and walks 6 km. How far and in which direction is he from the starting point?
questions.exp: North 6, then east 8, then south 6 cancels the north-south displacement, leaving 8 km east of the start.

questions.q: Find the next pair: AZ, BY, CX, DW, ?
questions.exp: The first letter moves forward and the second moves backward by one each time: D→E and W→V, giving EV.

questions.q: Heart : Pump :: Kidney : ?
questions.exp: The heart pumps blood; the kidney filters blood.

questions.q: Find the missing number: 2 → 6, 3 → 12, 4 → 20, 5 → 30, 8 → ?
questions.exp: The rule is n × (n + 1): 8 × 9 = 72.

questions.q: A is taller than B but shorter than C. D is taller than C. E is shorter than B. Who is the second tallest?
questions.exp: Order: D > C > A > B > E. The second tallest is C.

questions.q: If P means '+', Q means '×' and R means '−', then 8 Q 3 P 10 R 6 = ?
Given: A + B means A is the mother of B; A − B means A is the brother of B; A × B means A is the sister of B. Which expression shows that M is the maternal uncle of N?
questions.exp: M − K + N means M is the brother of K and K is the mother of N, so M is N's mother's brother (maternal uncle). The other options give an aunt or a mother.

questions.q: If + means ×, − means ÷, × means + and ÷ means −, then the value of 12 + 3 − 4 × 5 ÷ 2 is:
Which of the following is the odd one out?
questions.exp: Mercury, Venus and Mars are planets, whereas the Moon is a natural satellite.

questions.q:
Statements: All members of a club are adults. Some adults are chess players.
Conclusions: I. Some members are chess players. II. Some chess players are adults.
questions.exp: Some adults are chess players directly gives II. The chess-playing adults may not be club members, so I does not follow.

questions.q: Find the value of 36 ÷ 6 × 3 − 4 + 2 × 5.
In a certain code, CLOCK is written as EJQAM. How is TIMER written in that code?
questions.exp: Letters are shifted +2, −2, +2, −2, +2: T→V, I→G, M→O, E→C, R→T, giving VGOCT.

questions.q: Five persons P, Q, R, S, T sit in a row facing north. T is at the extreme left end and P is at the extreme right end. Q sits immediately to the left of R, and S sits to the left of Q. Who sits in the middle?
questions.exp: T is 1st and P is 5th. S, Q, R must fill places 2, 3, 4 in that order (S left of Q, Q immediately left of R). So Q is in the middle.

questions.q: What is the 8th letter to the left of the 5th letter from the right end of the English alphabet?
questions.exp: 5th from the right is V (position 22). 8th to its left is position 22 − 8 = 14, which is N.

questions.q: Find the next number: 3, 7, 16, 35, 74, ?
Find the next term: 100, 91, 83, 76, 70, ?
questions.exp: The differences are −9, −8, −7, −6, so the next is −5: 70 − 5 = 65.
